title: Crypto prices fall as ETF outflows resume, lending expands and stablecoin payments advance
paragraphs: Bitcoin traded around $64,100, down 1.1% over 24 hours, while ether fell 0.9% to about $1,797. The broader crypto market dropped 2.3% to roughly $2.18 trillion. The decline extended beyond the two largest assets: the aggregate market lost more ground than either bitcoin or ether. Prices remain under pressure even as financial institutions continue expanding their use of crypto infrastructure.

U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs recorded $239.9 million of net withdrawals in the latest completed session, reversing the preceding session's modest $7.9 million inflow. BlackRock's IBIT accounted for $209.5 million of the outflow. These redemptions show renewed selling through a major investment channel. They add context to bitcoin's weakness, although the flow figures alone cannot establish what caused the entire market move.

Coinbase expanded its crypto-backed borrowing product to New York, completing availability across all 50 U.S. states. Eligible residents can borrow USDC against bitcoin, ether or SOL, with Morpho supplying the lending infrastructure on Base. Coinbase told The Block the rollout followed state regulatory approval. Fixed-rate loans and several other collateral options remain unavailable in New York. The expansion brings on-chain credit to more customers through an established exchange, while retaining the collateral and liquidation risks of secured crypto borrowing.

The World Bank Group announced an initiative with Citi and Circle to explore regulated dollar stablecoins for development-finance payments. Citi would provide connections to banking infrastructure, while Circle would support minting and settlement in USDC. The work builds on FundsChain, which already tracks more than 350 projects across 96 countries. The stablecoin initiative is still exploratory. Faster, cheaper disbursements with better traceability could help development funds reach their recipients more efficiently.

At a Senate Agriculture Committee hearing, CFTC nominees Matthew Rowland and Nathan Anonick faced questions about oversight of sports-related prediction markets. Rowland expressed sympathy for state and tribal concerns; Anonick emphasized the agency's discretion and listening to stakeholders. Their nominations still require committee and full Senate votes. The hearing left the federal-state jurisdiction dispute unresolved, keeping uncertainty over which rules prediction-market operators will ultimately have to follow.

Our on-chain portfolio is worth about $56,700: $9,434 in the active treasury and $47,268 in the Safe. Its marked value fell $617, or 1.1%, from the previous comparable snapshot. Direct ARC holdings account for about $39,000, nearly 69% of the total, with another $5,546 in the Safe's WETH/ARC pool. ARC concentration remains the largest exposure. Beefy positions fell $25 to $1,801, while Curve rose $23 to $435. Ether exposure also runs through wallet balances, liquidity pools and lending collateral.

Across both wallets, Aave holds about $6,149 of WETH collateral against $3,150 of USDC debt. Health factors slipped from 1.89 to 1.87 in the treasury and from 1.51 to 1.49 in the Safe, reducing liquidation headroom. Fluid has about $1,218 of syrupUSDC and USDC collateral against $1,065 of USDC debt. Its net value is only $153, but the unchanged 1.03 health factor leaves very little room for adverse moves.
